headline: US stocks closed mixed as crude tumbled on US–Iran diplomacy hopes, with lingering AI-related pressure still in focus ahead of Apple earnings and US midterm elections
raw_text:
- The Dow Jones Industrial Average ($DJI) rose about 0.4% to 51,984, the S&P 500 ($SPX) slipped about 0.5% to 7,541, and the Nasdaq Composite ($COMP) fell about 1.1% to 25,164, as lingering AI-related pressure weighed on growth stocks.
- Crude oil (@CL) fell about 8% on prospects of a US–Iran diplomatic breakthrough that could ease Middle East supply risks, weighing on energy shares.
- Energy underperformed as ExxonMobil (XOM) fell about 4%, while the crude slide boosted consumer discretionary stocks, with Amazon (AMZN) up about 2% after Phillip Securities upgraded the shares to Buy, citing AI positioning.
- Mohawk Industries (MHK) climbed about 7% after announcing a share repurchase program.
- Oracle (ORCL) dropped about 9% after announcing a $10 billion stock offering as part of a $20 billion capital-raising plan to fund its AI cloud buildout.
- Marvell Technology (MRVL) slid about 13% and Lumentum (LITE) plunged about 19% after unveiling a $115 billion all-stock deal, a data center AI combination drawing comparisons to dot-com-era excess.
- ISM Manufacturing PMI showed expansion in October but with input prices still elevated, as investors continued to scrutinize heavy AI-related capital spending.
- Microsoft (MSFT) fell about 3% as it announced an expanded strategic collaboration with Lumen to co-sell enterprise AI-ready network solutions to joint customers.
- Apple (AAPL) is scheduled to announce Q4 results after the close with iPhone sales in focus, while Nasdaq 100 futures (@NQ) fell more than 1%.
- Investors now turn to tonight’s US midterm election results and another heavy batch of corporate earnings.
